questions.stem: A blown fuse must be replaced with one of:
options: Any size that fits
A higher rating
The same rating
A piece of wire
questions.explanation: A higher rating defeats the protection and can cause a fire.

questions.stem: Earth lamps on an insulated electrical distribution system are used to:
options: Show whether there is an earth fault
Show the engine speed on the switchboard
Measure how much load the generator carries
Measure the battery capacity remaining
questions.explanation: If one lamp dims or goes out and the other stays bright, the line with the dim lamp is earthed.

questions.stem: With two earth lamps on a two-wire insulated system, one lamp goes dark and the other glows brightly. This indicates:
options: The generator is overloaded on both lines
Both lines are healthy and well insulated
An earth fault on the line with the dark lamp
An earth fault on the line with the bright lamp
questions.explanation: A lamp on an earthed line has no voltage across it, so it goes dark.

options: Fuel directly into electricity
Electrical energy into mechanical energy
Mechanical energy into electrical energy
Heat energy into light and sound
questions.explanation: A generator or alternator does the reverse.

questions.stem: A generator or alternator driven by a diesel engine converts:
options: Electrical energy into heat in the windings
Fuel directly into electrical power
Electrical energy into shaft rotation
Mechanical energy into electrical energy
questions.explanation: The engine turns the machine, which produces electricity.

questions.stem: A navigation-light circuit on a vessel normally includes:
options: No fuse, so that it can never fail at sea
A connection through the bilge pump circuit
Its own protection and a way to show lamp failure
A switch shared with the galley and the cabin lighting circuit
questions.explanation: Nav lights are critical safety equipment, so the circuit is protected and monitored.

questions.stem: A circuit breaker keeps tripping when reset. You should:
options: Hold it closed until the fault burns clear
Fit a bigger breaker so it stops tripping
Find and fix the fault before resetting again
Reset it a few more times to see whether it will hold
questions.explanation: Repeated tripping means an overload or short. Find the cause.

questions.stem: Paralleling two generators allows them to:
options: Run at half speed to save fuel and wear
Share the load and change over without a blackout
Make DC from AC for the battery chargers
Charge the starting batteries only, not the main bus
questions.explanation: The incoming generator must match voltage, frequency and phase before connecting.

options: The total loss of main electrical power
A tripped bilge pump breaker
Low oil pressure on the generator
Loss of the navigation lights only
questions.explanation: Emergency power then supplies essential services.

questions.stem: The emergency bus is normally supplied from:
options: The main engine starter motor
The emergency generator or batteries
The shore connection only
The galley and domestic lighting circuit
questions.explanation: It serves emergency lighting, communications, steering and navigation lights.

questions.stem: If a ship's generator is overloaded, which circuits are shed first?
options: Navigation lights
Steering gear
Non-essential circuits
Fire pump
questions.explanation: A non-essential trip protects essential services.
